diagnosis.suspected_cause: The payment container has exited (Docker state: exited, unhealthy). Checkout's PaymentService/Charge calls fail with "no route to host" to 172.22.0.18:50051, so PlaceOrder fails and users can't check out.
alternatives: fraud-detection failure. It looks like an unrelated EventStream artifact and doesn't explain the checkout errors.
Kafka, opensearch or grafana memory pressure. All are stable, have not restarted, and have no link to the checkout errors.
A network or DNS fault that makes payment unreachable. Docker shows payment as exited, which makes this unlikely.
diagnosis.uncertainty: The reason payment exited is unknown. I had no payment logs or exit code, so I can't tell an OOM kill from a crash. The incident window is historical and I only saw live data. The fraud-detection 100% error rate comes from a single long-lived EventStream span ending with gRPC status 4. It looks like a streaming artifact, not a checkout cause, and I did not investigate it further. Kafka (94%), opensearch (91%) and grafana (70%, down from 89%) have high but stable memory. None has restarted, and all are still reporting. They look unrelated, but I could not rule out a minor contribution. Checkout errors are about 21% because only checkout flows reach the payment call.
diagnosis.next_step: Get the payment container's exit code and last logs (docker inspect and docker logs). Check for an OOM kill or a startup crash. Then restart it and confirm checkout recovers. Separately, keep watching kafka and opensearch memory.

proposals.reason: The payment container is in Docker state exited/unhealthy with restart_count 0. It stopped reporting about 1731 s ago. Checkout traces show errors originating in checkout, and the diagnosis links them to PaymentService/Charge failing with no route to host. A restart addresses a stopped process, which is the diagnosed cause.
proposals.risk: The exit cause (OOM, crash or config) is unknown. If it is a persistent fault, payment may exit again. Restarting changes the container's IP, which may matter if the address is cached. A restart will not fix bad code or configuration. The exit code and logs should be captured first (docker inspect / docker logs) before the restart overwrites the context. | catalog: In-flight requests to the service fail while it restarts (typically 5-20s). Does not fix bad code, configuration, dependencies or network faults.
proposals.expected_effect: The payment container starts and resumes reporting. Checkout's Charge calls succeed again and the checkout error rate falls from about 21% to baseline.
proposals.rollback: None available (restart is not reversible). If payment exits again, escalate with the exit code and logs.
